Mineral Springs.name: Mineral Springs
Mineral Springs.basicInfo:
The flowing stone-veins of The Stone Rise — clear mineral springs rising from the grey rock in cold, faintly metallic threads, pooling in terrace basins the moss-lichen has held for seasons. The water tastes of iron and clean cold, and drinking it settles the breath. Clay banks around the richest springs hold spirit minerals that glitter when the light is right.

Living Ecology: Translucent spring-snails browse crystal moss along the basins and leave empty pearl shells where the water turns. Moss-horn goats carry lichen spores between the upper and lower terraces.
Mineral Springs.hiddenInfo:
The springs rise along the dimension's structural grain — the water is drawn through Foundation Ridge's bedrock and emerges carrying trace spirit mineral, which is why it never stagnates. Mineral elementals surface at the deepest pools briefly and are harmless if ignored: they reform into the water if left undisturbed. Small hidden cave mouths thread the banks behind the springs — some stretch back into the hillside, some hold exposed ore seams, and at least one runs with porous rock that slowly filters mana-water. The Chamberlain has sampled all three springs monthly; their mineral content rises imperceptibly, a fact he logs as encouraging growth.

Ecological Continuity: Mineral elementals here are non-sapient expressions of water meeting dense spirit ore. Ignoring them leaves the springs undisturbed; observing one reveals no buried history or mineral map beyond what is physically visible.

High Outlook.name: High Outlook
High Outlook.basicInfo:
The great outcropping of The Stone Rise — a bare grey headland that, on clear days, sees the entire dimension from the Quiet Shore's pale coast to the Veiled Edge's shimmering curtain. On clouded days it still sees farther than anything else in the Demi-Plane, and the wind there carries the faint suggestion of every region at once. Mountain goats control the approach; cliff drakes nest below its southern face.

Living Ecology: Crystal-wing swifts circle below the crown while prairie seed caught on cliff-drake scales sprouts in cracks. On clear days, the connected water, root, wind, and migration corridors can be followed across all twenty-five tiles.
High Outlook.hiddenInfo:
The Outlook is the dimension's highest observation post — standing here, exactly oriented, trips an intentional quiet: the hum of the grass, the glow of the rift, the tint of the torii, all faintly audible at once, like a map made of sound. The Chamberlain climbs here before major reports. A natural cave behind the Outlook's crown was hollowed out by the dimension itself, dry and floor-smooth, apparently reserved — for what, even he does not guess. The cliff drakes below are territorial but know his hood.

Ecological Continuity: The sound-map conveys real, present ecological signals only. It cannot identify hidden actors, private conversations, motives, or events outside sensory reach.

Foundation Ridge.name: Foundation Ridge
Foundation Ridge.basicInfo:
The long grey ridgeline anchoring The Stone Rise — bedrock exposed at the spine, older-feeling than anything else in the young dimension. The moss here grows in precise bands, the air is stillest at its base, and sound behaves oddly near it: echoes fall a fraction early rather than late. It looks like any other ridge; it feels like keel timber.

Living Ecology: Bands of emerald, cobalt, and silver lichen make the bedrock's condition visible, while stone-boring beetles open tiny safe channels for springwater. The guardian's patrol leaves no damage or trail beyond a momentary hush.
Foundation Ridge.hiddenInfo:
The Ridge is the dimension's structural foundation — the bedrock on which the Demi-Plane is extrapolated from the Last Edge's anchor. Destabilizing it would set the whole dimension adrift; the Chamberlain does not know this. The Mana Heart's guardian entity patrols the ridge's perimeter when not at its post. Narrow passes thread over and beneath the ridge — some natural, some carved by no visible hand — and the rock is the dimension's densest: iron-rich, spirit-mineral-bearing, and slow to crack. Mining here should be done with reverence rather than appetite.

Ecological Continuity: Emerald indicates balanced flow, cobalt high pressure, and silver structural strain. These are observable conditions, not a replacement for the Mana Heart, Last Edge anchor, or development mechanics.

Twilight Pools.name: Twilight Pools
Twilight Pools.basicInfo:
The heart of The Mirror Mere — a spread of still pools under a sky that is forever twilight here, connected by gentle channels and ringed in reed-beds. The water faintly glows and holds reflection as if it remembers what stood before it; fish-sized lights drift beneath the surface, never quite taking shape. Everything in this place is reflected: the pools show what stands above them — and occasionally, what does not.

Living Ecology: Moonfin school beneath violet reeds, glass frogs pulse softly from lily pads, and opaline grit from the Veiled Edge turns in slow galaxies along the bottom. Ripples travel in pairs: the movement and its remembered echo.
Twilight Pools.hiddenInfo:
The pools regulate the dimension's mana circulation — absorbing excess during peaks, releasing during lulls; surface stillness is the Chamberlain's literal health check. But the water also remembers. Reflections sometimes outlast their originals — a bird flies off, its reflection stays. Focused gazing can trace these lingering images to hidden islands that surface in the shallows, or to temporary spirit paths that open across the channels at dusk, walkable until the reflection that anchored them fades. Mirror fish feed on the strongest memories in the water and their pearls are born from what is most dearly held.

Ecological Continuity: A pool can repeat a reflected movement or weather pattern after it passes, but it supplies no identity, motive, history, or dialogue that was never physically reflected.

Reflection Basin.name: Reflection Basin
Reflection Basin.basicInfo:
The Mirror Mere's largest single mirror — a broad, glassy expanse of water so still it doubles the twilight sky without a single tremor. Luminous reeds ring its edges; mirror-lotus bloom in those places where the water shows a thing and its reflection in perfect agreement. Visitors find their own reflections here clearer than reality: posture straightened, expression honest, tiredness falling away from the image if not the body.

Living Ecology: The Mere's largest unbroken surface holds the whole twilight sky and releases stored light through mirror-lotus roots at false dawn. Reflection herons patrol its shallows without disturbing more than one ring at a time.
Reflection Basin.hiddenInfo:
The Basin is the reservoir's deepest point and the circulation's master regulator — what shows still here means the whole dimension is stable. Submerged ruins lie beneath it, visible through the clear depth on quiet days: pale stonework that no one built, arranged as if some older idea of a temple preceded the dimension and the Mere remembered it. Visions stand whole in the still water — not predictions, but honest inspections: whoever looks long enough sees themselves as the dimension sees them, which is a kinder reading than most receive. Water spirits maintain the ruin's visibility by polishing the water from below, for reasons they keep politely to themselves.

Ecological Continuity: Visions require a concrete source—stored reflection, active divination, established magic, or actual observer. The basin never becomes a convenient omniscient screen.
